A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SplatSuRe. All 17 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original 4× and 8× super-resolution experiments, quantitative and qualitative comparisons, and threshold and SR-model ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results comparing unified and two-stage training in Appendix A.2 and Table 6.

M1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an optional unified pipeline: train on LR images for 5K iterations, compute fidelity scores and weight maps, then continue training with SR supervision for 25K iterations. This changes the training procedure while retaining the scoring mechanism, model architecture, and losses.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Tanks & Temples, Deep Blending, and Mip-NeRF 360 scenes at 4× and 8× super-resolution. The unified-pipeline experiment uses existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain 3DGS (LR), the StableSR-trained 3DGS baseline, Mip-Splatting, and SRGS. Renaming StableSR to 3DGS + StableSR clarifies the same comparator. New Table 6 compares training variants of SplatSuRe.

E3.justification: The new unified-pipeline experiment introduces a 5K LR plus 25K SR training schedule, totaling 30K iterations, stated to match single-stage baselines. Table 6 uses 4× SR and threshold 1.1. Existing splits, resolutions, metrics, and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 and Table 6 newly test whether a continuous training schedule preserves quality while avoiding separate-stage overhead. Existing threshold sensitivity analyses, SR-backbone ablations, and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its experimental results. The new table follows the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are unchanged. New Table 6 reports unified versus two-stage PSNR of 23.70 versus 23.81 on Tanks & Temples, 28.96 versus 29.01 on Deep Blending, and 26.69 versus 26.34 on Mip-NeRF 360. These are added comparisons under different training schedules, not corrections to existing scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical content is retained. Equation 8 disambiguates the dummy view index and writes the Gaussian index range explicitly; these are notation clarifications. No new theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about geometry-guided selective SR, fidelity scores, weight maps, and reconstruction quality. The unified schedule adds supporting evidence without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 now explicitly qualifies the radius ratio as an approximation to sampling frequency. Section 8 removes the specific smaller-upsampling/greater-consistency rationale and adds a future-work point about more view-consistent SR outputs. The principal limitations and scene-dependent interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the unified pipeline's 5K/25K schedule, when weight maps are computed, and the 30K baseline budget. Section 5 also corrects the implementation's 3DGS citation from reference 18 to reference 14. No hardware or measured training-time information is added.

R1.justification: The same 37 referenced works and related-work positioning are retained. Correcting the codebase citation does not add a cited work or revise the claimed relationship to prior methods.

P1.justification: v2 contains limited copyediting, shorter limitations and appendix prose, clearer baseline naming, and an inserted Appendix A.2 with subsequent renumbering. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6, rearranges Tables 4–5, adjusts table columns for the expanded baseline label, and corrects Table 1's caption from all to most metrics. Figures are retained. New Table 6 incorrectly bolds Mip-NeRF 360 FID 27.56 instead of the better 26.18.

improvement.justification: The unified-pipeline experiment adds useful evidence that SplatSuRe can retain comparable quality within a documented 30K-iteration schedule, addressing the original pipeline's extra training overhead. Clearer baseline naming and the corrected Table 1 caption also improve precision. The gain is limited: measured timing and uncertainty remain absent, and Table 6 introduces a small highlighting error.
